not additive in x and v, and an additive polynomial in each input reaches only ~3e-3.
- Exponential terms in v·e^(−x) and x·e^(−v) account for most of the remaining structure, but I could not pin down the exact closed form. Fractional powers and other single-term additions did not give a clean fit.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, x, v, params):
    w = 2*np.pi/20
    return (params[0] + params[1]*np.cos(w*t) + params[2]*np.sin(w*t) + params[3]*v
            + params[4]*v*np.exp(-x) + params[5]*v*np.exp(-x-v) + params[6]*v*v*np.exp(-x)
            + params[7]*np.log(x) + params[8]*v**3 + params[9]*x*np.exp(-v))
